newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Anglogold faces cost, competitive challenges - exec.
newsitem.headline: Anglogold faces cost, competitive challenges - exec.

text.p: One of the the world's largest mining companies, Anglo American Corp of South Afirca (Anglogold), set itself a multi-step plan to continue profitable development into the next century, delegates at a gold industry conference here heard on Tuesday.
Delegates at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett World Gold Confernece were told by Anglogold executive committee member Charles Carter that South Africa was now the world's highest cost major producer.
Consequently Anglogold has looked at containing costs through effective mining strategies, improved operating practives, higher productivity and better industrial relations.
Working South Africa's Witwatersrand Basin gold field at increasing depths and with incresing costs has led to questions being asked about the country's international competitiveness, he said.
Anglogold had three stategic objectives to answer these issues. It had to achieve global competiveness for its five operating mines, and develop "blue sky" potential , including ultra deep mining.
It also had to ensure there was sufficient wealth being created to take it into the next century.

The five Anglogold operating companies together produced 40.7 percent of South Africa's 495 tonnes of gold output last year and have proven reserves of 4,100 tonnes with further prospects at greater depth of about 1,500 tonnes, Carter said.
However, cash costs of production varied widely from $245 per ounce at Elandsrand to $314 at Freegold for a group average cash cost of $275.
These were "competitive cash costs" he said considering the great depth at which South African mining took place.
"Certainly in the South Afircdan context we are ahead of the pack," he said.

To reduce costs "smart' or team mining had been introduced and better labour productivity initiated at the Elandsrand mine to replace the multi-level parallel production processes with interdependent working.
The new work practices have been introduced in conjunction with new mining strategies.
The company has been restructured into clearly definied business units such as at Vaal Reefs where shaft working has been rationalized.
To make the most of the mines and increase their lives, mineral rights have been traded between the mining companies more vigorously than ever before, he said.
"In this way, these new patterns of ownership will lead to the profitable mining of previously sterlised reserves," he said.
Ultra deep mining is being developed at Western Deep levels which will extend the mine toa depth of 4,000 metres at a cost of Rand one billion.
The project will increase gold production over the life of the mine by 475 tonnes and the mine life by 13 years, Carter said.
Other research was exploring the possibility at mining at depths of between 3,500 meters and 5,000 metres at other Anglogold properties.

"The prospect of mining Witwatersrand Basin-type ore bodies at such depths is controversial. It also has some uncertainties. A range of technological challenges will have to be met," he told delegates.
